literal: Goodness of character is the goodness of the noble; other goodness is not included in any true goodness.
translation: The only true goodness of the noble is their goodness of character; any other kind of goodness is not worthy of being counted as goodness at all.
modern: நற்பண்புகளே சான்றோரின் சிறந்த நன்மையாகும்; மற்ற நன்மைகள் வேறு எந்த நன்மையிலும் சேர்த்து எண்ணத்தக்கவை அல்ல.
explanation: This couplet defines the essence of nobility (சான்றாண்மை) as being rooted solely in moral character. The poet contrasts 'குணநலம்' (goodness of character) with 'பிறநலம்' (other assets like wealth, strength, or beauty). He asserts that without a good character, no other quality can be counted as true goodness. The word 'உள்ளதூஉம்' uses poetic elongation to strongly emphasize that these other attributes do not even deserve to be placed in the category of virtue.
